purpose: Teach: 富豪/調教/落胆/軍部/反感/進入/出没/盗作

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、近代の富豪たちの慈善活動を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on the charitable activities of modern-era wealthy people, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm but measured. Genuine interest. Slight upward lilt at the end—inviting him to confirm. The steady attention of someone who reads her students closely.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、戦時下の馬の調教の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote my paper on the history of horse training during wartime.
lines.style: Quiet, direct response. A slight pause before answering—gathering his thought. Respectful but not stiff. The careful precision of someone choosing his exact words.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、敗戦時の国民の落胆を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper was about the people's despair at the time of defeat, wasn't it?
lines.style: Gently noting the shift. Curious, not correcting. Soft warmth underneath—she's tracking something. The tone of a teacher who notices when someone's work surprises her.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、軍部の独走による戦争への道を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote my paper on how the military's unchecked actions led the country toward war.
lines.style: Still calm and careful. A beat of sincerity—he means what he's saying about this topic. No defensiveness, just quiet conviction in the subject matter.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 政策への反感を生む要因を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You explored what factors generate public backlash against policy, didn't you?
lines.style: Leaning forward slightly—intellectually engaged now. The recognition of a thread connecting his work. Warmer, more animated than before. Seeing where he's going.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、国境を進入する不法移民の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote my paper on the history of illegal border crossings.
lines.style: Steady, unhurried. The tone of someone laying out a deliberate argument. No apology in his voice—just matter-of-fact commitment to the subject he chose.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、海賊が出没した時代を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, didn't your paper cover the era when piracy was rampant?
lines.style: A pause before the name—dawning recognition. Slightly slower pace. The careful tone of someone piecing something together. Reflective, not accusing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、学術界の盗作問題を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote my paper on plagiarism in academia.
lines.style: Direct, final. No hedging. The words land with quiet weight. Brief and clear—he's not elaborating because the point speaks for itself.
